observations.pairA_difference: Vertical position/attachment of the card relative to the menu bar: in 9E15 the card sits flush against the menu bar with a soft shadow gradient blending directly out of the dark menu-bar band into the card (no gap, top and bottom edges fade softly into the desktop grey); in C6D3 the whole card (including all its text) sits about 8px lower, separated from the menu bar by a flat strip of plain desktop-grey, and its top/bottom edges cut off sharply with no shadow blend.
observations.pairB_difference: Same property as pair A: 4B8A's panel is attached flush to the menu bar with a soft shadow blend at both the top and bottom edges; F03E's panel sits ~8px lower with a flat grey gap under the menu bar and hard, unblended edges top and bottom.
observations.content_lost: No — pixel-level comparison confirms identical text and elements in both pairs (Slack card wording in A, all five task rows / SOURCES / Stop / Continue-in-Workspace in B); only the vertical placement and edge/shadow treatment differ.

why.pairA: 9E15 is pulled up against the menu bar with a continuous soft shadow instead of a flat grey gap, so it reads as one structure growing out of the top edge rather than a card floating below it.
why.pairB: 4B8A shows the same attached, softly-shadowed edge treatment as 9E15, while F03E's gap and hard-cut edges make the panel read as a discrete window sitting on the desktop.
